I studied the system, then the docs. Everything below is derived from the code; the doc pass is step 6 only.

---

# What `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator` must do

**Absorption check (step 4), asked twice.** First pass over a five-item list: "a read is never refused, and the same Rules run on served content" was sitting inside the detection point's mechanism, and the `/reference-documents` routes had no home at all. Promoted it into the headline of #3 rather than opening a fifth point, because it is the same check running in the other direction, not a second check. Second pass over the resulting four: `Rule-Set-Version` on every answer is named in #2's headline, projects/suites passing through unchecked is named in #1's, the missing-tool and no-id escalations are named in #4's — no behaviour is left explained only inside another point's mechanism. Answer: no. Four stands.

**Count check: 4 key points, 4 diagrams.**

---

## #1 — A single door in front of TestLink, and the Rules stand in it

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/testlink-client.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/reference-document.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/docker-compose.yml`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/package.json`

**Mechanism.** `server.ts` composes exactly three things and hands them to `buildApp`: a `McpTestLinkClient` over `connectToTestLinkMcp` (a `docker run --rm -i dogkeeper886/testlink-mcp:1.6.0` child spoken to over stdio), a `PostgresStore` opened on `DATABASE_URL`, and the `StoredRule[]` that store answered. `buildApp` exposes 15 routes and nothing else: four on `/test-cases`, six on `/projects` and `/projects/:projectId/suites…`, two listings, two on `/reference-documents`. `PostgresStore` implements `DocumentStore` and adds `rules()`; it has no method that writes — the only SQL it ever issues is the `information_schema` probe in `hasSchema` plus three `select`s. `TestLinkClient` is the only path to TestLink, and `Queries.run` the only path to the database. `app.get('/projects')`, `listTestSuites`, `listTestCasesInSuite` return `TestLinkContent = unknown` straight through with no `findViolations` call and no `versioned()` wrapper — no Rule binds to a Project or a Suite. There is no reload route, no document-write route, and no route that reaches a filesystem path.

**Why it matters.** The generating agent cannot check its own prose, so the check is put where the agent cannot reach it. That only holds if the box is the agent's *whole* world: all of TestLink's structure has to be reachable through it (or the agent goes around), and none of the box's own configuration may be writable through it (or the agent loosens what rejects it). Both halves are structural here, not policed: the object the server holds cannot write.

**Diagram.**

```
   generating agent  ──── HTTP only, no filesystem, no SQL ────┐
                                                               ▼
 ┌───────────────────────── buildApp (Fastify) ──────────────────────┐
 │ POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /test-cases ......... Rules run               │
 │ GET  /reference-documents[/:id] ......... Rules run, read only    │
 │ /projects , /projects/:id/suites ........ served through, no Rule │
 │ (no reload route, no document write, no path parameter)           │
 └────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
          │ McpTestLinkClient                    │ PostgresStore
          ▼ (ToolCaller.call)                    ▼ (Queries.run: select only)
   stdio ─► testlink-mcp 1.6.0            rules │ rule_exceptions
              │                           reference_documents
              ▼                                  ▲
          TestLink                                │ psql, by the operator
```

**Contradicts.** `docs/agents/domain.md` states the project has no source tree. See step 6.

**Paths** (`[F]` = a fake cannot assert it):

| Caller action | Route through the box | Infra assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects` | `listProjects` → `list_projects` | TestLink's project list is returned unchanged; no Rule ran; the database received no statement |
| `GET /projects`, TestLink down | throws in `reach`/transport | 500; nothing in TestLink changed |
| `GET /projects`, TestLink answers an absence-worded error | `answer` → `absent` → `throw 'TestLink reported no Projects to list.'` | 500, not 404 — TestLink still holds its projects **[F]** |
| `POST /projects` valid | `create_project` | 201 + id; TestLink holds a new Project under that id carrying the `prefix` sent; body has **no** `ruleSetVersion` **[F]** |
| `POST /projects` missing `prefix` / unknown property / `"active": "true"` | ajv, `coerceTypes:false` | 400 `refusal:'schema'`; **no tool call was made**; TestLink holds no new Project |
| `POST /projects`, TestLink names no id | `idOf` throws | 500 `TestLink reported no id for the Project it created`; the caller must treat the write as unconfirmed **[F]** |
| `PUT /projects/:id` valid | `update_project` | 200 `{id}`; TestLink holds the changed settings; `false` and `""` survive `given()` and reach TestLink |
| `PUT /projects/:id` `{}` | `projectChangesSchema` `minProperties:1` | 400; no `update_project` call; Project unchanged |
| `PUT /projects/:id` absent | `place` → `absent` | 404 `TestLink holds no Project X`; nothing changed **[F: real wording]** |
| `PUT /projects/:id` on a TestLink without `tl.updateTestProject` | `place` falls through | 500 claimed by the README — unverified, see step 6 **[F]** |
| `DELETE /projects/:id?confirmPrefix=WL` correct | `delete_project` | 204; TestLink holds no such Project and nothing beneath it **[F]** |
| `DELETE /projects/:id` with no `confirmPrefix` | `deleteProjectSchema` querystring | 400; **no `delete_project` call**; the Project and all its content still there |
| `DELETE /projects/:id` wrong prefix | `reportsUnconfirmed` | 409; Project and every Suite/Case under it still there **[F: `/Confirmation failed/i`]** |
| `GET /projects/:id/suites` (± `parentSuiteId`) | `list_test_suites` | `parent_suite_id` is sent only when given (`given()`); listing returned unchanged |
| `GET /projects/:id/suites`, project absent | `absent` | 404 `TestLink holds no Project X`; nothing created **[F]** |
| `GET /projects/:pid/suites/:sid/test-cases` | `list_test_cases_in_suite(suite_id)` | the Suite's cases are returned **and `projectId` is never sent** — a mismatched Project in the path changes nothing |
| `GET …/test-cases`, suite absent | `absent` | 404 `TestLink holds no Test Suite X` **[F]** |
| `POST /projects/:pid/suites` valid | `create_test_suite` | 201 + id; TestLink holds the Suite under that Project, or under `parent_id` when given **[F]** |
| `POST …/suites` missing `name` | schema | 400; no tool call; no Suite created |
| `POST …/suites`, project absent | `absent` | 404; no Suite anywhere in TestLink **[F]** |
| `POST …/suites`, TestLink names no id | `idOf` throws | 500; write unconfirmed **[F]** |
| `PUT …/suites/:sid` valid | `update_test_suite` | 200 `{id}`; TestLink holds the new name/details |
| `PUT …/suites/:sid` with `{}` | `testSuiteChangesSchema` has **no** `minProperties` | 200 and `data:{}` reaches TestLink — the asymmetry with Projects is real; the Suite is unchanged **[F]** |
| `PUT …/suites/:sid` absent | `absent` | 404; **nothing was created** — an update reported as applied to a Suite that is not there would be a confirmation of nothing **[F]** |
| `DELETE …/suites/:sid` valid | `delete_test_suite(suite_id)` | 204; TestLink holds no such Suite and its Cases go with it **[F]** |
| `DELETE …/suites/:sid` absent | `absent` | 404; nothing else was removed **[F]** |
| Any of the above, TestLink unreachable | transport throws | 500; TestLink state unchanged in every case |
| Any request at all, in any order | whole app | the database log contains **no** `insert`/`update`/`delete` — only the four `select`s `PostgresStore` can issue **[F: needs the real store, not `StubDocumentStore`]** |
| `POST /reference-documents`, `POST /rules`, `POST /reload` | no route | Fastify 404, `Rule-Set-Version` header present; the database was neither read nor written |

---

## #2 — The Rules are the operator's rows, bound once at startup, and the server refuses to start rather than run without them — every answer then names them

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/setting.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/.env.example`

**Mechanism.** Four startup gates, each a throw before `app.listen`: `required()` on `DATABASE_URL`, `TESTLINK_URL`, `TESTLINK_API_KEY`, `TESTLINK_AUTHOR_LOGIN`; `store.rules()` answering `[]` → *"No enabled Rules are in the database, so the server will not start"*; `bindRules` → `checkStoredRule` per row → `refuse(problems)`, which prints **every** problem at once as `contentKind / field / ruleId: what is wrong`; and `JSON.parse` of `TESTLINK_MCP_ARGS` when `TESTLINK_MCP_COMMAND` is set. `hasSchema` asks `information_schema.tables` outright, so *schema never applied* answers "no Rules" rather than a stack trace, and is told apart from *database unreachable*, which throws out of `pg`. `rules()` selects `where enabled` — a disabled row is never read. `ruleSetVersionOf` hashes a canonical JSON per rule (`contentKind, field, ruleId, category, looksFor, flanked, reason, sorted exceptions`), sorted, sha256, first 12 hex — the row `id` and the database's ordering are deliberately excluded. `onSend` stamps `Rule-Set-Version` on **every** reply; `versioned()` adds `ruleSetVersion` to the body only where a Rule took part. `schema.sql` carries the constraints (`field_belongs_to_the_content`, `a_symbol_is_one_character` via `looks_for like '_'`, `only_a_symbol_is_flanked`, `unique (content_kind, field, rule_id)`); `checkStoredRule` re-checks all of them because "a type cannot be trusted about what a database answered with". `default-rules.sql` is 74 Terms + 15 Symbols × 5 Fields = 445 enabled rows, `on conflict … do nothing`.

**Why it matters.** This is the whole trust boundary made operational. Read-once means the agent cannot make the box forget a Rule by any sequence of requests; refuse-to-start means a mis-provisioned box never silently accepts everything; the derived version means a Violation logged today is still explainable against the exact Rules that produced it.

**Diagram.**

```
operator: psql -f schema.sql ; psql -f default-rules.sql ; npm run dev
   │
   ▼
required('DATABASE_URL' | 'TESTLINK_URL' | 'TESTLINK_API_KEY'
         | 'TESTLINK_AUTHOR_LOGIN')  ── unset/'' ─► "X is not set"   ✗ exit
   ▼
connectToPostgres ───────────────── unreachable ─► pg throws         ✗ exit
   ▼
PostgresStore.rules():  hasSchema? ── no ─► []
   select ... from rules where enabled order by id
   select rule, phrase from rule_exceptions where enabled
   ▼
   rules.length === 0 ───────────► "No enabled Rules ... Apply schema.sql" ✗
   ▼
bindRules → checkStoredRule ─ problems[] ─► "Rule Sets are invalid:" ✗ exit
   ▼                                          (every problem at once)
ruleSetVersionOf(rules) = sha256(canonical rows, sorted)[0..12]
   ▼
buildApp: onSend → header Rule-Set-Version   (every reply, 204 included)
          versioned(body) → ruleSetVersion   (only where a Rule judged)
   ▼
app.listen(PORT ?? 3000)   ── rules are never read again ──
```

**Contradicts.** ADR-0006's `rule_sets.source`/YAML, and ADR-0001's "baked into the deployed image". See step 6.

**Paths:**

| Caller action | Route through the box | Infra assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Operator starts with `DATABASE_URL` unset or `""` | `required` | process exits with `DATABASE_URL is not set, so this will not run.`; **nothing is listening on `PORT`**; no testlink-mcp container was started **[F]** |
| Same for `TESTLINK_URL`, `TESTLINK_API_KEY`, `TESTLINK_AUTHOR_LOGIN` | `required` | exit; no listener; note `TESTLINK_URL`/`TESTLINK_API_KEY` are read *after* the database, so a bad key fails only once the Rules already loaded **[F]** |
| Database unreachable | `connectToPostgres` | exit; no listener; TestLink never contacted **[F]** |
| Fresh database, `schema.sql` never applied | `hasSchema` false → `rules()` = `[]` | exit naming `schema.sql`; **the database still has no `rules` table — the server created nothing** **[F]** |
| Every Rule disabled | `where enabled` | same refusal; the rows are still present with `enabled=false`; nothing listening |
| A row with `field='title'` under `content_kind='testCase'` (schema bypassed) | `checkStoredRule` | exit listing `testCase / title / <id>: a Test Case has no Field by that name`; **the row is left exactly as written — nothing repairs or deletes it** |
| Several bad rows at once | `checkRules` collects then `refuse` | one message listing every problem; the operator fixes them in one pass, not one restart at a time |
| A Term row carrying `flanked` / a two-code-point "symbol" / empty `reason` / empty `rule_id` / `category='regex'` | `checkStoredRule` | exit with the matching message; rows untouched |
| Operator inserts a malformed row *with* the shipped schema applied | `schema.sql` CHECK constraints | `psql` refuses the `insert` at write time; the table gains no row **[F: needs a real/pg-mem Postgres]** |
| `TESTLINK_MCP_COMMAND=node` with `TESTLINK_MCP_ARGS` unset or not JSON | `testLinkMcp()` | exit `TESTLINK_MCP_ARGS must be a JSON list of arguments`; no process spawned |
| `TESTLINK_MCP_COMMAND` unset | default branch | `docker run --rm -i -e TESTLINK_URL -e TESTLINK_API_KEY dogkeeper886/testlink-mcp:1.6.0` — the tag is `expectedTestLinkMcp`, never `latest` **[F]** |
| testlink-mcp image missing / container cannot start | `connectToTestLinkMcp` | exit; the port is never bound **[F]** |
| Clean start, then N requests | `rules()` called once in `server.ts` | the query log shows the `rules`/`rule_exceptions` selects **exactly once** for the life of the process, whatever N is **[F]** |

## #3 — A Rule is literal text matching over one Field, reported whole — and the same check runs on what is served as on what is written, where it never refuses

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/reference-document.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql`

**Mechanism.** `findViolations(content, ruleSets)` walks each Field's `RuleSet`. A `TermRule` builds `matcherFor` — the phrase regex-escaped, every whitespace run replaced by `\s+`, flags `giu` — and keeps a hit only where `standsAsWord`, i.e. `isOutsideAWord` on both sides, where a word runs through `\p{L}\p{N}_-` (so `utilises` and `re-associates` survive a ban on `utilise`/`associates`). A `SymbolRule` scans with `indexOf` and, when `flanked==='whitespace'`, keeps only hits where `isGap` holds both sides, the Field edge counting as a gap. Then `suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)` — the Rule's *own* Exceptions, found the way a Term is but *without* the word test — and `isSuppressed` drops a hit whose whole span falls inside an Exception span. A `Violation` is `{field, rule, reason, text, offset}` with `text` in the casing actually found and **no suggested replacement**. `bound.testCase` and `bound.referenceDocument` are separate `Map`s, so a Rule cannot reach the other kind's Fields. Writes: `reject()` logs one `warn` per Violation carrying `{ruleSetVersion, field, rule}` and answers `422`. Reads: `GET /test-cases/:id` and `GET /reference-documents/:id` attach `violations` *beside* `testCase`/`document` and never refuse, however many fired; reads log nothing.

**Why it matters.** Determinism is the product — the same submission is answered word for word every time because nothing is counted or read back. And the read side is not a nicety: the read path is the only channel by which the agent sees prior content, so serving a Reference Document written in the very wording the Rules catch, *without* saying so, would teach the fingerprint straight back into new cases. Refusing the read instead would put the content out of reach of the only party who can fix it.

**Diagram.**

```
Field value ──► for each Rule in bound[kind].get(field)
                 │
    type 'term'  ├─► matcherFor: escape, /\s+/ between words, flags giu
                 │     └─ standsAsWord?  [\p{L}\p{N}_-] either side → no
    type 'symbol'└─► indexOf(symbol)
                       └─ flanked==='whitespace' ? isGap(left) && isGap(right)
                 │
                 ▼
              fired[] ── .filter(!isSuppressed) ──► Violation
                            ▲                        {field, rule, reason,
             suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)   text, offset}
             (match must fall wholly inside a span)    no replacement

POST/PUT /test-cases  : violations.length>0 → reject() 422 + one warn line
                        per Violation, and testlink is never called
GET /test-cases/:id   ─┐
GET /reference-docs/:id┘ violations served BESIDE the content, never refused
```

**Contradicts.** README's HTML/offset caveat is honest and matches the code (no wrapping anywhere in `McpTestLinkClient.createTestCase`).

**Paths:**

## #4 — Five answers, told apart on purpose — and absence is read only out of TestLink's own words

**Ground truth:** `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts` (`setErrorHandler`, `reject`, `nothingThere`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/mcp-testlink-client.ts` (`answer`, `place`, `reportsAbsence`, `reportsUnconfirmed`, `reportsMissingTool`, `deniedIn`, `idOf`), `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/tool-caller.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/stdio-tool-caller.ts`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/testlink-client.ts`

**Mechanism.** Five distinguishable shapes, each with a different owner. **400** `{refusal:'schema', message}` from `setErrorHandler` on `error.validation`, with `coerceTypes:false` so a wrong type is refused rather than converted — it carries *no* `violations`, so it cannot be misread as a Rejection. **422** `{violations, ruleSetVersion}` — no `refusal` key. **404** `{message: 'TestLink holds no …'}` from `nothingThere` — no `refusal`, no `violations`, no version, because nothing was refused and no Rule took part. **409** only on `DELETE /projects/:id`, when `reportsUnconfirmed` matches `/Confirmation failed/i`, checked *before* absence so the interlock is not mistaken for a missing Project. **500** for everything else. The whole judgement lives in `McpTestLinkClient.answer`/`place`: an `isError` result, or a `200`-shaped reply whose first record carries `code` + `message` (`reportedProblem`), goes to `place`, which tries `alsoTheCallers` → `reportsMissingTool` (`/Unknown tool/i` → *"testlink-mcp does not provide X, so it is older than the 1.6.0 this client calls"*) → `reportsAbsence` (`/does not exist|not found/i` → `absent`) → **throw**. Escalation is the default: an unrecognised failure is an outage, never "not there". Absence is read only from what TestLink said *about the call*, never from served content — a Test Case may legitimately say "the file does not exist" and must not vanish. Two further outage shapes guard the write: `deniedIn` (a cleanly-arrived reply with `status:false`) throws *"TestLink did not complete X"*, and `idOf` throws *"TestLink reported no id for …"* when the created id is absent, `0` or `""` — an unconfirmed write is never answered as a success.

**Why it matters.** The caller is an agent, and each shape demands a different act: fix your JSON, fix your prose, fix your id, restate the prefix, retry later. Collapse any two and the agent loops — told a Case is "not there" when TestLink is merely down, it stops looking for a Case that exists.

**Diagram.**

```
request
  │ ajv (testCaseSchema | newProjectSchema | projectChangesSchema
  │      | deleteProjectSchema | newTestSuiteSchema | testSuiteChangesSchema)
  │                                    ── fails ──► 400 refusal:'schema'
  ▼                                                  (no tool call at all)
findViolations(...) ── fires ────────────────────► 422 violations[] + version
  ▼                                                  (nothing written)
McpTestLinkClient.answer(tool, args)
  ├ isError  |  reportedProblem(code+message) ──► place(tool, message)
  │     ├ reportsUnconfirmed /Confirmation failed/i ──► 409  (delete_project)
  │     ├ reportsMissingTool /Unknown tool/i ────────► 500 "older than 1.6.0"
  │     ├ reportsAbsence /does not exist|not found/i ► 404 nothingThere()
  │     └ nothing matched ───────────────────────────► 500 outage (default)
  ├ deniedIn(status:false) ──────────────────────────► 500 "did not complete"
  ├ idOf(): no id, or 0, or "" ──────────────────────► 500 "reported no id"
  └ content ──────────────────────────────────────────► 200 | 201 | 204
```

**Contradicts.** README's `tl.updateTestProject` claim rides on a branch that does not exist. See step 6.

**Paths:**

| Caller action | Route through the box | Infra assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Body missing `name` or `summary` on `POST`/`PUT /test-cases` | `testCaseSchema.required` | 400; `findViolations` never ran; **no `create_test_case` call**; TestLink holds nothing new |
| Body with an unknown Field (`steps`) | `additionalProperties:false` | 400; nothing written |
| `"summary": 42` | `coerceTypes:false` | 400 rather than a coerced `"42"` being written; TestLink holds nothing new |
| Schema refusal on any of the 7 schema'd routes | `setErrorHandler` | body has `refusal:'schema'` and **no `violations` and no `ruleSetVersion`**; header still present; backend untouched |
| Any Rejection | `reject` | body has `violations` and `ruleSetVersion` and **no `refusal`**; TestLink issued no id |
| Any absence, on any of the 12 routes that can be absent | `nothingThere` | 404 `TestLink holds no …`; **no `refusal`, no `violations`, no `ruleSetVersion`**; nothing created, changed or removed **[F: the real failure wording]** |
| `POST …/suites/:sid/test-cases` into a Suite TestLink does not hold | `createTestCase` → `absent` | 404 naming **both** `Test Suite X in Project Y` — TestLink does not say which is missing; **no new Test Case anywhere in TestLink** **[F]** |
| `DELETE /projects/:id` with a wrong prefix | `reportsUnconfirmed` before `reportsAbsence` | 409, not 404 and not 500; the Project and its whole tree survive **[F]** |
| TestLink unreachable on any route | transport throws → `reply.send(error)` | 500, not 404 — a retryable outage; backend state unchanged |
| Database unreachable on `/reference-documents[/:id]` | `pg` throws | 500, not 404; the two are told apart by status code alone |
| TestLink fails with wording the client does not know | `place` default branch | 500 `TestLink could not be reached through X` — **never** answered as absence **[F]** |
| A read whose *content* contains "does not exist" | `reportsAbsence` is applied to reported problems only | 200 serving that text; TestLink still holds the Case **[F]** |
| testlink-mcp older than 1.6.0 | `reportsMissingTool` | 500 naming the version — read as a version fault, not as TestLink being down; TestLink is reachable throughout **[F]** |

| A create TestLink answers with `id: 0` or `id: ""` | `idOf` | 500; the caller does not receive an id nothing is held under **[F]** |
| `DELETE /test-cases/:id` on a held Case | `delete_test_case` | 204 with an empty body **and the `Rule-Set-Version` header still on it**; TestLink no longer holds it **[F]** |
| `DELETE /test-cases/:id` on an absent id | `absent` | 404; nothing else was removed **[F]** |
